speaker: Unknown
en: We're no longer in this era of good enough is fine.
zh: 我们不再处于“差不多就行”的时代了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good enough is not enough.
zh: 差不多是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's mediocre.
zh: 那是平庸。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to win in the game of software, you need to differentiate through design.
zh: 如果你想在软件游戏中获胜，你需要通过设计来脱颖而出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Craft matters.
zh: 工艺很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are a couple lessons you've learned for founders that are thinking about startup ideas?
zh: 对于那些正在思考创业点子的创始人，你学到了哪几条经验？

speaker: Unknown
en: We started the company August 2012, started working hardcore at Figma in June 2013.
zh: 我们于 2012 年 8 月创办了公司，2013 年 6 月开始在 Figma 全力以赴地工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, summer of 2017 we made our first money.
zh: 然后，2017 年夏天我们赚到了第一笔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't do that.
zh: 别那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get to market faster.
zh: 更快地推向市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish we had.
zh: 我希望我们当时那样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a counterintuitive decision you made along the journey of Figma?
zh: 在 Figma 的旅程中，你做过什么反直觉的决定吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: FigJam.
zh: FigJam。

speaker: Unknown
en: About a month before the launch of FigJam at Config, it was like, "Okay, we built a thing."
zh: 在 Config 大会上发布 FigJam 之前大约一个月，情况就像，“好吧，我们构建了一个东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just lacking something.
zh: 它就是缺了点什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The soul isn't there.
zh: 灵魂不在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go differentiate by making FigJam fun.
zh: 让我们通过让 FigJam 变得有趣来做出差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: The team was like, "What?
zh: 团队就像，“什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to make fun our differentiator?"
zh: 我们要让‘有趣’成为我们的差异化点？”

speaker: Unknown
en: In retrospect, it was absolutely the right move.
zh: 回过头看，这绝对是正确的举措。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's talk about Figma Make, the use cases that seem to be emerging in this world of AI and app prototyping are prototypes for product teams.
zh: 让我们谈谈 Figma Make，在这个 AI 和应用原型设计的世界中似乎正在浮现的用例是产品团队的原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: PMs are no longer saying to the designer, "Hey, can you draw this thing out for me?"
zh: PM（产品经理）不再对设计师说，“嘿，你能帮我把这个东西画出来吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: That frees up designer time to go explore more deeply the stuff they need to go into and it allows anyone to add to that first conversation of, where should we go?
zh: 这腾出了设计师的时间去更深入地探索他们需要深入研究的东西，并且它允许任何人参与到第一场对话中，即我们应该去哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which function maybe is most in trouble?
zh: 哪个职能可能最麻烦？

speaker: Unknown
en: It all depends on the way that things play out from here.
zh: 这一切都取决于事情从这里开始的发展方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you have to believe is your organization gets better as models get better.
zh: 你必须相信的是，随着模型变得更好，你的组织也会变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have we seen productivity increases?
zh: 我们看到生产力的提升了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but that is not something that has made our new headcount we want for engineering to go down.
zh: 是的，但这并没有让我们希望的新工程编制人数下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're hiring.
zh: 我们正在招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my guest is Dylan Field.
zh: 今天，我的嘉宾是 Dylan Field。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dylan is the CEO and co-founder of Figma, one of the most beloved and used products in the world.
zh: Dylan 是 Figma 的 CEO 和联合创始人，Figma 是世界上最受喜爱和使用最广泛的产品之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know a single product team that doesn't use and love Figma, which is extremely rare.
zh: 我不知道有哪个产品团队不使用并喜爱 Figma 的，这极为罕见。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our chat, we talk about how Dylan kept the company focused and motivated after the Adobe deal fell through, how he's most evolved as a leader over the past 13 years, his vision for Figma Make, and how it's different from the other products out there.
zh: 在我们的对话中，我们谈论了 Dylan 是如何在 Adobe 交易告吹后保持公司的专注和动力的，他在过去 13 年中作为领导者的最大演变，他对 Figma Make 的愿景，以及它与市面上其他产品的不同之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: How he expects product building to look in five years, what good product taste looks like, his strategy for launching new product lines, and how market size is the wrong way to think about it, and so much more.
zh: 他预期 5 年后产品构建会是什么样子，什么是良好的产品品味，他推出新产品线的策略，以及为什么市场规模是思考它的错误方式，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: This conversation was so delightful.
zh: 这段对话非常愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dylan is such a nice, interesting, curious human, and I always have such a great time talking to him.
zh: Dylan 是一个非常善良、有趣、充满好奇心的人，我和他交谈总是很开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guarantee you'll both enjoy this conversation and find a lot of nuggets to take back to your team.
zh: 我保证你会喜欢这段对话，并发现很多可以带回给团队的宝藏。

speaker: Unknown
en: A big thank you to Mihika Kapoor, Robert Bye, Yuhki Yamashita, Akshay Kothari, and Zach Lloyd for suggesting topics for this conversation.
zh: 非常感谢 Mihika Kapoor、Robert Bye、Yuhki Yamashita、Akshay Kothari 和 Zach Lloyd 为本次对话建议话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you enjoy this podcast, don't forget to subscribe and follow it in your favorite podcasting app or YouTube.
zh: 如果你喜欢这个播客，别忘了在你最喜欢的播客应用或 YouTube 上订阅和关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: It helps tremendously.
zh: 这有很大帮助。

en: Head on over to Lennysnewsletter.com and click product pass.

zh: 有了这个，我为您带来 Dylan Field。

en: 1.3%, it's a small number but in the right context it's a powerful one.
zh: 1.3%，这是一个很小的数字，但在正确的语境下，它是一个强大的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stripe processed just over $1.4 trillion last year.
zh: Stripe 去年处理了刚超过 1.4 万亿美元的金额。

speaker: Unknown
en: That figure works out to be about 1.3% of global GDP.
zh: 这个数字约占全球 GDP 的 1.3%。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a lot, but it's also just 1.3%.
zh: 这很多，但也只有 1.3%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stripe handles the massive scale and complexity of many of the world's fastest growing enterprises, including 78% of the Forbes AI 50 and more than half of the Fortune 100.
zh: Stripe 处理着世界上许多增长最快的企业的大规模规模和复杂性，包括 78% 的 Forbes AI 50 和超过一半的财富 100 强。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a reason I've had more leaders from Stripe on this podcast than any other company.
zh: 这就是为什么我请 Stripe 的领导者来这个播客的次数比其他任何公司都多的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know how to build great products that scale and that people love.
zh: 他们知道如何构建可扩展的、人们喜爱的伟大产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stripe is also a lot more than just payments.
zh: Stripe 也远不止是支付。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've also got a category leading billing solution and a highly optimized checkout experience built specifically to increase your checkout conversion.
zh: 他们还拥有业界领先的计费解决方案和高度优化的结账体验,专门为提高您的结账转化率而构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enterprises like Atlassian, Figma, and Urban use Stripe to create fully branded and customized checkout pages with access to more than 125 global payment methods.
zh: 像 Atlassian、Figma 和 Urban 这样的企业使用 Stripe 创建完全品牌化和定制化的结账页面,并能使用超过 125 种全球支付方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Join the ranks of industry leaders like Salesforce, OpenAI, and Pepsi that are using Stripe to grow faster and grow GDP.
zh: 加入像 Salesforce、OpenAI 和 Pepsi 这样的行业领导者行列,他们正在使用 Stripe 以实现更快增长并增长 GDP。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn how Stripe can help your business grow at Stripe.com.
zh: 请在 Stripe.com 了解 Stripe 如何帮助您的业务增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dylan, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Dylan,非常感谢你能来这里,欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, Lenny, thank you for having me back.
zh: Hey, Lenny,谢谢你再次邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to see you.
zh: 很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also great to see you too, Dylan.
zh: 见到你我也很高兴,Dylan。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last time we chatted, this was right after the Adobe deal didn't work out.
zh: 上次我们聊天时,就在 Adobe 交易没谈成之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, you're a public company, a public CO, congrats on that.
zh: 现在,你是一家上市公司,一家 public CO,恭喜你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically, post-Adobe deal falling through, the journey you guys have taken, it was quite unusual.
zh: 具体来说,在 Adobe 交易告吹之后,你们团队走过的这段历程,是非常不寻常的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You almost sold the company to Adobe for a lot of money and then the deal fell through.
zh: 你们差点把公司卖给 Adobe,卖了一大笔钱,然后交易就告吹了。

speaker: Unknown
en: My understanding is it fell through because the UK government regulatory boards just didn't want it to happen.
zh: 我的理解是,交易告吹是因为英国政府监管委员会就是不想让它发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that why it fell through?
zh: 那就是它告吹的原因吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the story there, by the way?
zh: 顺便问一下,那边的 story 是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, various regulators did not like the deal and had arguments against it.
zh: 是的, various regulators 不喜欢这笔交易,并对此提出了反对意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: No need to go into those and whatnot.
zh: 没必要深入讨论那些以及诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, yeah, it was a long process, 16 months.
zh: 但是,是的,这是一个漫长的过程,16 个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: Adobe is an incredible company, a lot of respect for that team, and very interesting to, even in this constrained context where you can't plan out a road map or they can't give you instructions and stuff like that of, here's what you should do or not do.
zh: Adobe 是一家不可思议的公司,非常尊重那个团队,非常有趣的是,即使在这个受限的背景下,你不能规划路线图,或者他们不能给你指示以及诸如此类的事情,比如你应该做什么或不应该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just seeing them operate through the regulatory process even was fascinating.
zh: 即使只是看着他们通过监管过程运作也是迷人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, it was intense and I'm really glad we kept our foot on the pedal, gas pedal, and just kept accelerating forward rather than grinding to a halt.
zh: 但是,是的,这很紧张,我真的很高兴我们kept our foot on the pedal,油门踏板,并且只是继续向前加速而不是逐渐停滞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we're able to exit this deal that didn't work out and go into launching Dev Mode and really pushing on how do we expand our platform in a big way.
zh: 因为我们能够退出这笔没有 work out 的交易,并进入推出 Dev Mode,并真正推动如何以big way扩展我们的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been I think just further acceleration of pace from there.
zh: 我认为从那里开始,节奏进一步加快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really proud of the team for how they handled that and also how they're in focus now, and it's a real honor to be on this team.
zh: 我为团队如何处理了这一切感到骄傲,也为他们现在的专注感到骄傲,能成为这个团队是一种真正的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me actually ask you about that exact thing.
zh: 让我实际上问问你关于那件确切的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most leaders, most teams would get super discouraged, and demoralized, and distracted by something like this.
zh: 大多数领导者,大多数团队会因此变得超级沮丧、士气低落和分心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, there was a bunch of money ready to be wired to their bank accounts.
zh: 基本上,有一大笔钱准备汇到他们的银行账户里。

speaker: Unknown
en: This deal was going to sell.
zh: 这笔交易本来是要卖的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "Oh, amazing."
zh: 就像是,“噢,太棒了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, it doesn't happen.
zh: 然后,它没有发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Easy for people just to get, "Oh, no, what the hell's going on here?
zh: 人们很容易变得, “噢,不,这到底是怎么回事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why am I working here?
zh: 我为什么要在这里工作?

speaker: Unknown
en: All these news about us."
zh: 所有关于我们的新闻。”

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you very specifically keep people focused and keep momentum up, as you said, almost accelerate it to this very successful IPO?
zh: 你究竟是如何让人们保持专注并保持势头的,正如你所说,几乎将其加速到了这次非常成功的 IPO?

speaker: Unknown
en: Communication is obviously a big part of it, first of all.
zh: 显然,沟通是其中很大的一部分,首先。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have some legal constraints in the regulatory process, but to however degree we really could, we would do just quarterly check-ins and updates on here's how things are going.
zh: 你在监管过程中有一些法律约束,但在我们无论如何 really could 的程度上,我们会做季度检查和更新,关于事情进展如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point those became more frequent.
zh: 在某些时候这些变得更频繁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, every few weeks.
zh: 是的,每隔几周。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was check-in towards the end and at some point it was like, "Okay, the path is narrowing."
zh: 在最后是check-in,在某个时点就像是,“好的,路径正在变窄。”

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point I was able to share with people, "Hey, the path is narrow."
zh: 在某个时点我能够与人们分享,“嘿,路径很窄。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone picked up on that.
zh: 并不是每个人都get到了那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people still had in their heads, this is going to go through, of course, it's just a matter of time.
zh: 有些人仍然在脑海中认为,这会通过的,当然,这只是时间问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think tactically one thing that was really important coming out of the process, we announced the company the day after we went on break, basically.
zh: 我认为战术上,在流程结束后,有一件事真的很重要,我们在放假后的第二天宣布公司,基本上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, Friday we went on a winter break, not everybody, but most of the company was on vacation for probably a week and a half, two weeks for the winter.
zh: 就像是,周五我们去度冬假了,不是所有人,但公司的大部分人可能在休假一个半,两周过冬。 [[95] ] 当然有些人仍在进行支持和保持服务器运行以及所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some folks are of course still on for support and keeping servers up and all that.
zh: 当然有些人还在负责支持和保持服务器运行以及所有这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think that the Monday after that we all went on break, reconvene everyone, just establishing, "Hey, this didn't happen, here's what's next."
zh: 但是,是的,我认为在我们大家都去休假后的那个周一,重新召集所有人,只是建立,“嘿,这没有发生,接下来就是这个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, coming back from break, and one thing we did was a program we called Detach, which is a Figma pun for detaching components.
zh: 然后,从休假回来,我们做的一件事是一个名为 Detach 的程序,这是 Figma 的一个双关语,用于detaching components。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was just a way for us to say, "Hey, look, maybe you joined and you thought you were joining Adobe, and surprise, you're at this hard charging startup."
zh: 但这只是我们说的一种方式,“嘿,看,也许你加入了,你以为你加入了 Adobe,结果惊喜,你是在这个hard charging startup。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Or, maybe after a long time of working at Figma you're tired.
zh: 或者,也许在 Figma 工作了很长时间之后,你累了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's okay.
zh: 没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anyone wants to take three months of severance, and this is not a forever goodbye, you can reapply in six months, it's fine.
zh: 如果有人想拿三个月的遣散费，而且这不是永远的告别，你可以在六个月后重新申请，没关系的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're free to do so and we're still in good terms.
zh: 你可以自由这样做，而且我们仍然关系良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: A little bit over 4% of the company took us up on that.
zh: 公司里有略多于 4% 的人接受了这个提议。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it was also like, along with that reinforcing of the pace that we're going to be operating at, the challenge in front of us that we can go and meet, and the opportunity, and making sure people are aware of that too.
zh: 但我认为这也像是，连同对我们将要保持的节奏的强化，我们能够面对的挑战，以及机会，并确保人们也意识到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "Okay, great, if you're bought in, let's go.
zh: 就像是，“好吧，很好，如果你买账了，那就走吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're not there, that's okay."
zh: 如果你不在那里，那也没关系。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It was actually really interesting to see the folks that did take it, how many of them ended up doing career changes.
zh: 看到接受提议的人，实际上非常有趣的是，他们中有多少人最终进行了职业转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some folks went from sales to politics or something.
zh: 有些人从销售转行去从政或做其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: People went in totally different directions sometimes.
zh: 有时候人们走向了完全不同的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was a reset moment not just for the company but also for some folks for their lives and their careers, and that's been fascinating to watch how that's worked out for them.
zh: 我认为这不仅是公司的重置时刻，也是一些人他们生活和职业的重置时刻，看到这对他们产生了怎样的结果一直很迷人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, I didn't know you guys did that, a fork in the road you might call it.
zh: 哇，我不知道你们这么做了，你可能称之为岔路口。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of this hard-charging concept, I want to get your insights on how you've been able to maintain the pace that you guys have maintained.
zh: 说到这种硬核冲刺的概念，我想了解你是如何能够保持你们所保持的这种节奏的见解。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys are over 10 years old at this point.
zh: 你们现在已经有 10 多年历史了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How old is Figma at this point?
zh: Figma 现在几岁了？

speaker: Unknown
en: We started in August 2012, so we just hit 13.
zh: 我们于 2012 年 8 月开始，所以我们刚满 13 岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: 13 years.

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly, things continue to move fast.
zh: 显然，事情继续快速发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: From an outsider's perspective, it feels very much like a startup and everyone I meet from Figma feels like they work at a startup.
zh: 从局外人的角度来看，这感觉非常像一家初创公司，我在 Figma 遇到的每个人都觉得他们在一家初创公司工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do to keep that pace up?
zh: 你做什么来保持这种节奏？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're looking at timelines or you're thinking about what to work on, I think first of all, the selection of problems is really important, and making sure we're motivated.
zh: 当你审视时间表或你在思考要做什么工作时，我认为首先，问题的选择真的很重要，并确保我们有动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then, after you get into that, if things are not converging, dragging out, you have to be willing to move on and move to other projects.
zh: 但是，在那之后，如果事情没有收敛，拖延下去，你必须愿意继续前进并转移到其他项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: If timelines are maybe not well reasoned through from first principles and perhaps there's padding that has been well intentionally added by different folks, you have to understand fully, okay, what are the assumptions of how long things will actually take and what is a padding?
zh: 如果时间表可能没有从第一性原理出发经过充分推理，或许有不同的好心人加了填充时间，你必须充分理解，好吧，实际需要多长时间的假设是什么，什么是填充时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, really work through that with the team.
zh: 然后，真的要和团队一起解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, I think keeping a flatter org is helpful.
zh: 另外，我认为保持更扁平的组织结构是有帮助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd also just say that path dependency is super important.
zh: 我还要说的是，路径依赖超级重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of times that folks will assume that there's some requirement that actually is not a requirement, or they won't assume that something's required and it actually is super required and really important, and we have to slow down.
zh: 很多时候人们会假设有一些实际上不是要求的某种要求，或者他们不会假设某事是必须的而实际上它是必须的且真的很重要，我们必须慢下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, last thing I had to say, you always have to keep in mind tech debt and there might be, when you're moving slow, systematic reasons for that.
zh: 然后，我要说的最后一件事，你必须始终记住技术债务，当你移动缓慢时，可能有系统性的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make sure that you're not grinding to a halt because things are built the wrong way or you rush to get something out, and you need to go and fix the underlying infrastructure or way that you built it in some form?
zh: 你如何确保你不会因为事情构建错误或你匆忙推出某事而停滞不前，你需要去修复底层基础设施或你以某种形式构建它的方式？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that you can actually get the overall speed up and you have to have the right balance between addressing tech debt quality but also pushing these forward.
zh: 这样你实际上可以获得整体加速，你必须平衡解决技术债务质量与推动这些事情之间的正确平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is awesome.
zh: 这太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so let me follow up in a couple of these.
zh: 好的，让我跟进其中的几点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This point about finding padding and where people may be over estimating how long something might take, how does that look?
zh: 关于找到填充时间和人们可能高估某事需要多长时间这一点，这看起来怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that you going in and just like, "This feels way longer than it should."
zh: 是你走进去然后就像，“这感觉比应该的要长得多。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it you finding a deputy of just like, "Hey, can you just make sure this estimate looks reasonable?"
zh: 还是你找到了一个副手就像，“嘿，你能确保这个估算看起来合理吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you actually approach that generally?
zh: 你实际上通常如何处理这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's just coming from a place of curiosity, and the more that you can actually understand about underlying work that's being done, the better decisions that you can make, but also the more you can challenge and say, "Okay, is it really going to take this long, and if so, why?
zh: 是的，我认为这只是出于好奇心的地方，你关于正在做的工作的实际底层了解得越多，你能做出的决定就越好，而且你也可以更多地挑战并说，“好吧，真的需要这么长时间吗，如果是，为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something I'm missing?"
zh: 有什么我遗漏的吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Oftentimes, there are things I'm missing and things are either harder because we have additional constraints I don't know about in order to get something out and at scale.
zh: 通常，有一些我遗漏的事情，事情要么更难，因为我们有我不知道的额外约束，以便为了推出某事并达到规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes that's not the case and actually assumptions are being made that are maybe not quite correct or maybe we're understaffed and we need to go resource scenario better.
zh: 有时情况并非如此，实际上正在做出的假设可能不太正确，或者可能我们人手不足，我们需要更好地进行资源规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's all sorts of things that can come out of that and it's not always just me, to your point, plenty of others in the team will dig into things too.
zh: 所有各种各样的事情都可能由此产生，而且总是不仅仅是我在做这件事，正如你所说，团队中的其他人也会深入挖掘事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the people on my team are much more expert in their area than I am, so I'm always leaning on folks to learn.
zh: 我团队中的大多数人都在他们的领域比我更专业，所以我总是依靠大家来学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: You made this other point about people moving on to other projects.
zh: 你做了关于人们转移到其他项目的另一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 那是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it just like, okay, this investment is not worth our time anymore.
zh: 只是像，好吧，这项投资不再值得我们的时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just put all these resources on different project.
zh: 让我们把所有这些资源都放在不同的项目上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or, is it more, this person's not right for this initiative, let's have him work on something else.
zh: 或者，更多的是，这个人不适合这个倡议，让我们让他做点别的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both.
zh: 两者都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are I think a lot of people who when you put them on the thing that they are super interested and fired up about will outperform your wildest imagination of what's possible.
zh: 我认为有很多人，当你把他们放在他们超级感兴趣和充满热情的事情上时，他们的表现会超出你对可能的想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: Put in the wrong effort where they're not motivated, yeah, they will be fine.
zh: 把精力放在错误的地方，他们没有动力，是的，他们会还行。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can actually understand what people care about and then map them with their interests to the right projects, it is just so helpful.
zh: 如果你能真正理解人们关心什么，然后将他们的兴趣与合适的项目匹配起来，这真是太有帮助了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds so obvious, but people don't always do it and we're not perfect to this either.
zh: 听起来显而易见，但人们并不总是这么做，我们在这方面也并不完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're always trying to make sure that we're learning and understanding folks in what they care about.
zh: 我们始终努力确保我们正在学习和了解人们关心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that I always feel also about Figma is the culture is incredibly fun and interesting and unique and just good.
zh: 关于 Figma 我也一直感觉到的一件事是，这种文化非常有趣、独特且令人愉悦，就是很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine a lot of people just joined Figma because the culture is so good.
zh: 想象一下，很多人加入 Figma 只是因为文化太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard to maintain a strong consistent culture over time.
zh: 随着时间的推移，要保持强大一致的文化真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said you've been around for 13 years now.
zh: 你说你已经在这个圈子里 13 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember at Airbnb there was a lot of things that the founders did to maintain that culture and evolved it over time.
zh: 我记得在 Airbnb，创始人做了很多事情来维持那种文化，并随着时间的推移发展它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what you do to maintain that culture, keep it strong, and also just adjust as the company grows.
zh: 我很好奇你做了什么来维持这种文化，保持它的强大，并且随着公司的发展进行调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the first thing that's most important is just the people.
zh: 我认为最重要的一点首先是人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, it's so obvious, but what is a culture?
zh: 同样，这很明显，但什么是文化？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's a collection of people and their rituals and the way they engage, and the informal and formal ways that people organize, but it all starts with people.
zh: 嗯，它是人及其仪式、他们互动的方式、以及人们组织和组织的非正式和正式方式的集合，但这一切都始于人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that consistently, possibly because of the problem domain that we tackle and how creative and design-forward the product is, we attract an extremely creative group of folks applying to Figma that are very maker-oriented.
zh: 我认为一直如此，可能是因为我们要解决的问题领域以及产品是多么具有创造力和以设计为导向，我们吸引了一群极其有创造力的人申请 Figma，他们非常以制造者为导向。

speaker: Unknown
en: They like to build things, they like to create things.
zh: 他们喜欢构建东西，他们喜欢创造东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is across functions.
zh: 这跨越了所有职能。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just design, engineering, product, research, it's the entire company.
zh: 不仅仅是设计、工程、产品、研究，它是整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think reinforcing that, making sure that of course we are not just looking for that, there's more we look for for people that are going to excel at their craft, that have a growth mindset, that have self-awareness, that have humility, high integrity.
zh: 我认为加强这一点，确保当然我们不仅仅是在寻找那个，还有更多我们要寻找的东西，即那些能在自己的手艺上出色的人，那些拥有成长型思维的人，那些有自我意识、有谦逊、高正直的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the things that are obvious, but also, we do care about people that want to push their craft forward in a big way.
zh: 所有这些显而易见的事情，而且，我们确实关心那些想要极大地推动自己手艺发展的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It all starts with I think that impulse to make, and we try to celebrate it too.
zh: 一切都始于我认为那种制造的冲动，我们也试图庆祝它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make a Reek is an example of that where like a week long company hackathon and the only prompt is, make Figma better in some way.
zh: Make a Reek 就是一个例子，比如为期一周的公司黑客马拉松，唯一的提示是，以某种方式让 Figma 变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That could be clearing your inbox if you want to not make something that week, if you're drained.
zh: 如果那周你不想制造东西，如果你精疲力尽了，那可能是清理你的收件箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the more interesting stuff is not clearing the inbox, it's teaming up with others.
zh: 但更有趣的事情不是清理收件箱，而是与他人组队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pushing the frontiers of what's possible for Figma.
zh: 这是推动 Figma 可能性的前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about Mihika earlier, before we started recording I think, and she had gathered a group of people to create Figma slides that came out of Make a Reek.
zh: 我们之前谈到了 Mihika，我认为是在我们开始录制之前，她聚集了一群人来创建 Figma slides，这源于 Make a Reek。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of our products and our most important features have come out of Make a Reek setting, and the demos at the end are just so good.
zh: 我们的许多产品和最重要的功能都源于 Make a Reek 的设置，最后的演示真是太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They always fire us all up and really just show a comprehensive picture of, wow, there are so many things we can do.
zh: 它们总是让我们所有人都兴奋起来，真的只是展示了一幅全面的图景，哇，我们可以做这么多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, let's focus in and figure out what is it that's going to move the company forward most.
zh: 现在，让我们集中精力弄清楚什么是推动公司发展的最重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an awesome guest post by Mihika that I'll point to in the show notes, where she describes the whole process of building Figma slides, also an awesome podcast episode, if folks aren't familiar with her.
zh: 我们有一篇很棒的由 Mihika 撰写的客座文章，我将在节目注释中指出，她在其中描述了构建 Figma slides 的整个过程，还有一期很棒的播客节目，如果人们不熟悉她的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked to Mihika and a bunch of other people actually preparing for this conversation to see where I want to poke at.
zh: 我和 Mihika 以及其他许多人谈过，实际上是为了这次对话做准备，看看我想探讨什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The co-founder of Notion, Akshay Kothari, had a really good quote that I want to share and I have a question about this.
zh: Notion 的联合创始人 Akshay Kothari 有一个非常好的引用，我想分享一下，我对此有一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, "Dylan is among the nicest humans, probably has an NPS of 100.
zh: 他说，“Dylan 是最和善的人类之一，NPS 可能有 100。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's incredibly warm and yet he's got this crazy drive energy underneath.
zh: 他非常温暖，然而他在内心深处拥有这种疯狂的驱动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's a total killer.
zh: 他是个十足的杀手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just look at the success of Figma in the business.
zh: 只要看看 Figma 在业务上的成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: This combination is quite rare.
zh: 这种组合非常罕见。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does he manage to do both?"
zh: 他是如何做到这两点的？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's very kind of Akshay.
zh: 嗯，Akshay 真的很客气。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think my NPS is a hundred, but it's very kind.
zh: 我不认为我的 NPS 是一百，但这很客气。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think I've always loved competition and games.
zh: 看，我想我一直热爱竞争和游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I definitely self-select into games that I think I can win.
zh: 我肯定会自我选择那些我认为我能赢的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: For that reason, I was never very athletic and stayed away from the team sports as a kid because nothing drives me more crazy than there's a game I'm playing and I cannot win it.
zh: 正因为如此，我从来不是很好运动，小时候远离团队运动，因为没有什么比我在玩一个游戏而我无法赢它更让我疯狂的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prior to Figma, yeah, I definitely care very much about doing well for just that own sense of competition that we have, but also for the company.
zh: 在 Figma 之前，是的，我确实非常关心做得好，只是为了我们自己拥有的那种竞争感，也是为了公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, all the competitors that I've met along the way are wonderful people.
zh: 而且，一路上我遇到的所有竞争对手都是很棒的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have the same often thing that they're trying to go for.
zh: 他们通常有相同的目标，他们正在努力争取。

speaker: Unknown
en: The same change they want to make in the world, around empowering folks and advocating for design.
zh: 他们想在世界做出的同样的改变，关于赋予人们力量和倡导设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: End of the day they're almost entirely an amazing set of humans as you get to know them.
zh: 归根结底，当你了解他们时，他们几乎全都是很棒的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that there's no reason you can't have good sportsmanship while being competitive.
zh: 是的，我认为没有理由你在保持竞争力的同时不能有良好的体育精神。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like the Dylan we're seeing in this conversation and in every conversation is the Dylan that everyone sees internally.
zh: 我觉得我们在这次对话和每次对话中看到的 Dylan 就是每个人在内部看到的那个 Dylan。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not another hardcore Dylan that just everyone hates.
zh: 没有另一个每个人都讨厌的硬核 Dylan。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I think Akshay's quote tells us.
zh: 这就是我认为 Akshay 的引用告诉我们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope so.
zh: 我希望如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I definitely get into intense modes sometimes, as we all do, but I try to keep it level when I can.
zh: 我肯定有时会进入紧张模式，就像我们大家一样，但我尽可能试着保持平稳。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious how your leadership style has evolved over the years.
zh: 我很好奇你的领导风格这些年来是如何演变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Figma has been around for 13 years, as we've been talking about.
zh: Figma 已经存在 13 年了，正如我们所谈到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you were to compare, say, Dylan 10 years ago to the Dylan of today, what would you say is most different?
zh: 如果你要比较一下，比如说，10 年前的 Dylan 和今天的 Dylan，你会说最大的不同是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of zero to one on management that I need to learn.
zh: 在管理方面有很多从 0 到 1 的东西我需要学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came in never having managed a team and it turns out you can just call yourself a CEO, but I might've had some leadership skills.
zh: 我刚进来时从未管理过团队，结果发现你可以自称 CEO，但我可能有一些领导技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I had a lot to learn on the management side.
zh: 我想我在管理方面有很多要学的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Until Sho started as first director of engineering, then he moved into product later, he's just a very multi-talented guy, but he taught me a ton about management.
zh: 直到 Sho 开始担任第一任工程总监，后来他转到了产品部门，他只是一个非常多才多艺的人，但他教了我很多关于管理的知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been our theme.
zh: 这一直是我们的主题。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the people I've hired as leaders I've learned so much from.
zh: 我聘请的许多领导者我都从他们身上学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But outside of that zero to one, where I just had a lot to understand about how to manage folks, I think on the leadership side, it's the same lessons over and over again.
zh: 但除了那个从 0 到 1 的过程，我那时有很多关于如何管理人的东西要理解，我想在领导力方面，这些教训一次又一次地重复。

speaker: Unknown
en: I keep learning them and then forgetting and worrying them again, and I think I get a little better every time.
zh: 我不断学习然后忘记，然后再担心它们，我想每次我都会变得好一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of them is just, how do you unpack context?
zh: 但其中之一就是，你如何拆解上下文？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you get the context you've got in your head and really unpack it for a group?
zh: 你如何获得你脑中的上下文，并真正为一个群体拆解它？

speaker: Unknown
en: Another is, how to make sure that you're showing up in a way that folks know that we're all working towards the same goal?
zh: 另一个是，如何确保你表现出的方式让人们知道我们都在朝着同一个目标努力？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I said, I can definitely get into intense mode where I'm asking a lot of questions, but it's always from a place of trying to understand or trying to figure out something together, and making sure I show up the right way there is important.
zh: 就像我说的，我肯定可以进入紧张模式，我会问很多问题，但这总是出于试图理解或试图一起弄清楚某些事情的目的，确保我在那里以正确的方式表现是很重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I would say just clarity is the thing that I circle back to the most right now.
zh: 是的，我会说目前我回来最多的东西就是清晰度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clarity around where are we all going as a company, but also clarity for any individual team.
zh: 关于我们作为一家公司去向何方的清晰度，但也包括对任何单个团队的清晰度。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's a lack of clarity, how do I help clear the way, but also how do I teach others just to be as direct as possible to unpack that, to create the clarity themselves too?
zh: 如果缺乏清晰度，我如何帮助扫清道路，还有我也如何教别人尽可能直接地去拆解它，以便他们自己也能创造清晰度？

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are just some of the things that I count the most.
zh: 这些只是我最看重的一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are so many threads I'd love to follow here.
zh: 这里有很多线索我很想继续深究。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just this last one on clarity is such an important skill for leaders, for product builders.
zh: 也许只是最后这关于清晰度的一点，这对于领导者、对于产品构建者来说是一项如此重要的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything specific there that you try to do to improve your clarity?
zh: 你有没有什么特别的事情是你试图做的来提高你的清晰度？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always these areas where things feel murky, and sometimes it's because you just haven't done the work to understand them yet fully.
zh: 总是存在这些领域，事情感觉模糊不清，有时是因为你还没有做工作去完全理解它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes it's because no one's done the work to understand them fully.
zh: 有时是因为没有人做工作去完全理解它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's your job as a leader to always try to investigate those areas, push on them, and if something's not adding up, really ask the hard questions and not shy away from them.
zh: 我认为作为领导者，你的工作就是总是试图调查这些领域，推动它们，如果有些事情不合适，真正问出棘手的问题，不要回避它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that too many people are of this instinct of like, "Rah, rah."
zh: 我认为太多人有这种本能，就像，“冲啊，冲啊。”

speaker: Unknown
en: We always got to be positive or something.
zh: 我们总是必须保持积极或类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not about positive or negative, it's about, well, do we understand it?
zh: 这不是关于积极或消极，而是关于，好吧，我们要理解它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have we had the hard conversations?
zh: 我们进行过艰难的对话了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have we thought through the hard trade-offs here?
zh: 我们是否在这里仔细思考过艰难的权衡？

speaker: Unknown
en: I just try to keep pushing through that until we get to a point of, "Okay, we at least know what we're trading off.
zh: 我只是试着一直推动它，直到我们达到这样一个点，“好吧，我们至少知道我们在权衡什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have unpacked and now we know where we're going, and everyone's on the same page, even if we don't all agree."
zh: 我们已经拆解了，现在我们知道我们要去哪里，而且每个人都达成共识，即使我们不是都同意。”

en: I've been using the word product builder a lot more actually too.

en: It just feels like such a better term instead of product manager or engineer.

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this question of, which function will be most taken on by other functions?
zh: 有这个问题，哪个职能将最被其他职能接管？

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, do you think engineers and PMs will become, engineers and designers will become more PM-y, PMs will become more design-y?
zh: 例如，你认为工程师和产品经理会变得，工程师和设计师会变得更像产品经理，产品经理会变得更像设计师吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which function maybe is most in trouble, is one way to put it.
zh: 哪个职能可能最麻烦，这是一种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that it all depends on the way that things play out from here.
zh: 我认为这完全取决于事情从这里的发展方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, no one knows if we're on S-curve of progress or an exponential curve, or actually we're on that end of the S-curve, but it's about to become exponential because of a new architecture breakthrough.
zh: 当然，没有人知道我们是否处于进步的 S 曲线上，还是指数曲线上，或者实际上我们处于 S 曲线的末端，但因为新的架构突破它即将变成指数级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the only thing that we know is that models will improve.
zh: 我认为我们唯一知道的是模型会改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will it be incremental?
zh: 会是增量式的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Will it be exponential?
zh: 会是指数级的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Somewhere in between, who knows?
zh: 介于两者之间，谁知道呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: But what you have to believe is that you get better as models get better.
zh: 但你必须相信的是你会随着模型的变好而变好。

en: Your organization gets better as models get better.
zh: 你的组织会随着模型的变好而变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now at least we're nowhere near, at least at Figma, to the point where our demand for development for example is satiated.

en: Have we seen productivity increases?
zh: 我们看到生产力的提升了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, mild to moderate, but that is not something that has made our new headcount we want for engineering to go down.

speaker: Unknown
en: We're hiring, and on the product side, yeah, judgment matters just as much as ever.
zh: 我们正在招聘，而且在产品方面，是的，判断力仍然和以往一样重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ability to rally a team around a vision matters just as much as ever.
zh: 凝聚团队围绕愿景的能力仍然和以往一样重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Design I think grows only more important in this role, in this world.
zh: 我认为设计在这个角色中，在这个世界中只会变得更加重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in this world where software can be created more easily, design matters so much and designers matter so much.

en: I think designers are going to be the leaders of the future and I think that more designers need to step into that leadership role.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like an eval of a bunch of 40 different actual jobs, and a few of them were like, the AI is a few percentage points away from humans, it turns out.

speaker: Unknown
en: Interestingly, those jobs are not yet disappearing, which tells us there's hope that this may actually not destroy a ton of jobs, maybe it gets to a hundred percent and then we're screwed, but it doesn't seem like it.
zh: 有趣的是，这些工作还没有消失，这告诉我们有希望这实际上可能不会破坏大量工作，也许它达到 100% 然后我们就完了，但看起来不像。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think first of all it's like evals are hard.
zh: 我认为首先这就像 evals 很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talked about that earlier.
zh: 我们之前谈过那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Secondly, the jobs don't just stay the same.
zh: 其次，工作不会一成不变。

speaker: Unknown
en: They change.
zh: 它们会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take prompting, and as an engineer there's a range of prompting abilities.
zh: 拿提示词来说，作为一名工程师，有一系列的提示词能力范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way you discreetize and split up your tasks matters.
zh: 你离散化和拆分任务的方式很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you assume that a model can do more than it can do, then you're going to have a bad time.
zh: 如果你假设模型能做到比它实际能做的更多，那你就会过得很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: You really got to understand where its capabilities lie.
zh: 你真的得理解它的能力在哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that changes some of the skills needed to be maximally efficient as an engineer.
zh: 我认为这改变了一些作为工程师达到最大效率所需的技能。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Only 17%, and I think it's pretty encouraging actually that folks understand viscerally that this is not coming for you, and that I think the next thing will be about as tools improve, as models improve, how do you improve and adapt?

speaker: Unknown
en: There might be points where it's slow and points where it's rapid, but overall I'm quite excited.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 就像在个人层面上，你可以把它看作你学习和探索世界和人类意识的路径，或者你可以用它来做你的作业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, I've got a point of view on which one's better.
zh: 显然，我对哪个更好有自己的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it'll be interesting to see how people adapt and grow.
zh: 我认为看人们如何适应和成长会很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this answer.
zh: 我喜欢这个回答。

zh: 只是给你一个机会做宣传，你们在招什么职位？

zh: 你们对什么人感兴趣？

zh: 我们正在招聘大多数职位，但我想说，首先，如果你热爱难题并且如果你真的对如何做感兴趣，如果你是 Figma 的用户并且你在想，“天哪，他们可以做得好得多。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Come talk to us.

speaker: Unknown
en: We want people who have a bold point of view on how we can always be improving, and vision for where they want to take Figma.
zh: 我们想要那些对我们如何总能改进有大胆观点的人，以及对他们想把 Figma 带向何方有愿景的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we have our own point of view too, so we'll have to think through it together.
zh: 显然，我们也有自己的观点，所以我们需要一起思考。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但我们在寻找高判断力的个人，那些会卷起袖子做很多事情的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether they're ICs or managers, and people that are going to get in the details and perfect their craft because we know that's how we're going to win, is by having the best craft, the best design.
zh: 无论他们是独立贡献者还是管理者，以及那些会深入细节并完善他们手艺的人，因为我们要知道那将是我们赢的方式，就是拥有最好的手艺，最好的设计。

zh: 你在日常生活或工作中发现有什么使用 AI 的方式真的很有趣，也许对人们学习有帮助？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, is there anything along those lines or just something you can share about AI in your life?
zh: 我不知道，有没有类似那样的东西，或者只是关于你生活中的 AI 你可以分享的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Beyond the obvious, I think there are certain domains where it does really well.
zh: 除了显而易见的，我认为在它做得非常好的某些领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: I definitely oftentimes will ask an AI model about a legal question now before I call a lawyer, because I find it's not replacing my call with a great lawyer, but it does inform my point of view.
zh: 我现在肯定经常会在给律师打电话之前问 AI 模型一个法律问题，因为我发现它并没有取代我和优秀律师的通话，但它确实为我的观点提供了信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be careful about when you do that.
zh: 你在什么时候做这件事必须小心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your conversation with AI is not the same as your conversation with a lawyer, but I think that any place where you're going to consult an expert but can come in more informed, that is interesting.
zh: 你与 AI 的对话不同于你与律师的对话，但我认为，在任何你要咨询专家但可以带着更多信息进入的地方，那都是有趣的。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, all the combinations of that and give it a title and give it a description.

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I've got a full table for those six traits, the entire possibility space of what that character sample might look like.
zh: 现在，我有了那六个特征的完整表格，那个角色样本可能看起来像什么的整个可能性空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just builds intuition about a possibility space in a different way if you do that.
zh: 如果你那样做，它只是以不同的方式建立对可能性空间的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something I think is a process that people could learn from and adapt more.
zh: 我认为这是人们可以学习并适应更多的一个过程。

en: Are you telling us you're writing a book?
zh: 你是在告诉我们你在写书吗？

en: No, I'm not writing a book.
zh: 不，我不是在写书。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fun to see where the model's going to go and when they're off the rails.
